squawweed: The golden ragwort. See under Ragwort.
squinting: a. & n. from Squint, v. -- Squint"ing*ly, adv.
squirrel: 1. (Zoöl.) Any one of numerous species of small rodents belonging to the genus Sciurus and several allied genera of the famly Sciuridæ. Squirrels generally have a bushy tail, large erect ears, and strong hind legs. They are commonly arboreal in their habits, but many species live in burrows.
squacco: A heron (Ardea comata) found in Asia, Northern Africa, and Southern Europe.

squamose: 1. Covered with, or consisting of, scales; resembling a scale; scaly; as, the squamose cones of the pine; squamous epithelial cells; the squamous portion of the temporal bone, which is so called from a fancied resemblance to a scale. 2. (Anat.) Of or pertaining to the squamosal bone; squamosal.
squamoid: Resembling a scale; also, covered with scales; scaly.
squib: 1. A little pipe, or hollow cylinder of paper, filled with powder or combustible matter, to be thrown into the air while burning, so as to burst there with a crack. | To throw squibs; to utter sarcatic or severe reflections; to contend in petty dispute; as, to squib a little debate. squabchick: A young chicken before it is fully fledged. [Prov. Eng.]
squareness: The quality of being square; as, an instrument to try the squareness of work.
squaloid: Like or pertaining to a shark or sharks.
squiralty: Same as Squirarchy. That such weight and influence be put thereby into the hands of the squiralty of my kingdom. Sterne.
squeezing: 1. The act of pressing; compression; oppression. 2. pl. That which is forced out by pressure; dregs. 3. Same as Squeeze, n., 2.

squaretoed: Having the toe square. Obsolete as fardingales, ruffs, and square-toed shoes. V. Knox.
squireen: One who is half squire and half farmer; -- used humorously. [Eng.] C. Kingsley.
squalid: Dirty through neglect; foul; filthy; extremely dirty. Uncomed his locks, and squalid his attrie. Dryden. Those squalid dens, which are the reproach of large capitals. Macaulay.
squall: A sudden violent gust of wind often attended with rain or snow. The gray skirts of a lifting squall. Tennyson. Black squall, a squall attended with dark, heavy clouds. | To cry out; to scream or cry violently, as a woman frightened, or a child in anger or distress; as, the infant squalled.
squid: 1. (Zoöl.) Any one of numerous species of ten-armed cephalopods having a long, tapered body, and a caudal fin on each side; especially, any species of Loligo, Ommastrephes, and related genera. See Calamary, Decacerata, Dibranchiata.
squiggle: To shake and wash a fluid about in the mouth with the lips closed. [Prov. Eng.] Forby. | To move about like an eel; to squirm. [Low, U.S.] Bartlett.
squeegeeroller: A small India-rubber roller with a handle, used esp. in printing and photography as a squeegee.
squalor: Squalidness; foulness; filthness; squalidity. The heterogenous indigent multitude, everywhere wearing nearly the same aspect of squalor. Taylor. To bring this sort of squalor among the upper classes. Dickens.

squamellate: Furnished or covered with little scales; squamulose.
squirehood: The rank or state of a squire; squireship. Swift.

squawman: A white man who has married an Indian squaw; sometimes, one who has gained tribal rights by such a marriage; -- often a term of contempt. [Western U. S.]

squad: 1. (Mil.) A small party of men assembled for drill, inspection, or other purposes. 2. Hence, any small party. | Sloppy mud. [Prov. Eng.] Tennyson.
squali: The suborder of elasmobranch fishes which comprises the sharks.

squalidness: Quality or state of being squalid.
squinteyed: 1. Having eyes that quint; having eyes with axes not coincident; cross-eyed. 2. Looking obliquely, or asquint; malignant; as, squint-eyed praise; squint-eyed jealousy.

squiery: A company of squires; the whole body of squires. Note: This word is found in Tyrwhitt's Chaucer, but is not in the modern editions.

squeaker: 1. One who, or that which, squeaks. 2. (Zoöl.) The Australian gray crow shrile (Strepera anaphonesis); -- so called from its note.
squeal: 1. To cry with a sharp, shrill, prolonged sound, as certain animals do, indicating want, displeasure, or pain. 2. To turn informer; to betray a secret. [Slang] | A shrill, somewhat prolonged cry.
squally: 1. Abounding with squalls; disturbed often with sudden and violent gusts of wind; gusty; as, squally weather. 2. (Agric.) squirr: To throw with a jerk; to throw edge foremost. (old) [Written also squirr.] Addison.

squabbler: One who squabbles; a contentious person; a brawler.

squeeze: 1. squirarch: One who belongs to the squirarchy. -- Squir"arch*al, a.

squir: To throw with a jerk; to throw edge foremost. (old) [Written also squirr.] Addison.

squarer: 1. One who, or that which, squares. 2. One who squares, or quarrels; a hot-headed, contentious fellow. (old) Shak.
squamiform: Having the shape of a scale.
squalodon: A genus of fossil whales belonging to the Phocodontia; -- so called because their are serrated, like a shark's.
squirely: Becoming a squire; like a squire.

squinance: 1. (Med.) The quinsy. See Quinsy. (old) 2. (Bot.) A European perennial herb (Asperula cynanchica) with narrowly linear whorled leaves; -- formerly thought to cure the quinsy.
